title: Foundry Local: Cutting-Edge AI experiences on device with ONNX Runtime/Olive — Emma Ning, Microsoft

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 98%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: Foundry Local is presented as a developer platform with CLI, SDKs, and a management service that engineers use to build cross-platform local AI applications. The platform is explicitly positioned as a tool for software builders creating on-device AI experiences across Windows and macOS. The talk covers both building applications with SDKs and running models locally on-device in production scenarios. The talk assumes familiarity with AI and inference concepts but introduces Foundry Local from scratch with live demos. Recorded conference presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair featuring slides and live CLI and application demonstrations. All eight evidence anchors are graded as said_in_transcript with direct excerpts from the talk.

summary: Emma Ning, a Principal PM in Microsoft's AI Framework team, introduces Foundry Local, a solution for building cross-platform applications powered by local AI. She motivates local AI over cloud AI through four reasons: handling low bandwidth or offline environments, privacy and security for sensitive data, cost efficiency for high-volume inference, and real-time latency. She notes local AI is now viable due to hardware advancements (modern GPUs, NPUs), leaner optimized models (Phi, DeepSeek variants), and runtime-level optimization techniques. Microsoft combines existing assets into Foundry Local: Azure AI Foundry (70,000+ organizations, 1,900+ models), ONNX Runtime (10M+ downloads/month with significant performance advantages over PyTorch), and Windows's massive device scale. The architecture uses ONNX Runtime at the base for hardware acceleration, a management service for hosting models on client devices, connectivity to Azure AI Foundry for on-demand model downloads, a CLI for model exploration, and SDKs for application integration. The platform works across Windows and macOS with deeper Windows platform integration, and partners with Nvidia, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm for hardware acceleration. Over 100 customers participated in private preview. Customer testimonials from Pieces (CEO Savo) highlighted improvements in memory management, time to first token, and tokens per second over alternatives like Llama.cpp and Ollama. Another customer demonstrated hybrid solutions combining Foundry Local with local speech-to-text for sensitive data. Live demos showcased CLI commands (foundry model list, foundry cache list, foundry model run), hardware-specific model variants (CPU, CUDA, integrated GPU, NPU), and approximately 90 tokens per second for Phi-3.5 1.5B. A cross-platform document summarization app using the JavaScript SDK was demonstrated running identically on Windows and macOS with different model choices (Phi-4 mini vs Qwen). The talk concluded with a detailed local agent demo: an OCR agent consisting of Phi-3.5 mini model and two MCP servers (file system and OCR), which autonomously searched for a receipt, extracted text via OCR, and computed the total amount. Ning noted local models are generally less capable than cloud models but unlock significant potential, and invited attendees to sign up for the agent feature private preview.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Motivation for Local AI
sections.summary: Emma Ning introduces herself and poses the question of why local AI is needed despite powerful cloud AI. She presents four key reasons: offline/low-bandwidth operation, privacy and security for sensitive data, cost efficiency for high-volume inference, and real-time latency requirements.

sections.title: Readiness of Local AI
sections.summary: Explains why local AI is now viable: decades of hardware progress (modern GPUs, NPUs), leaner optimized models from companies (Phi, DeepSeek variants), and advanced runtime-level optimization techniques converging to make local AI a reality.

sections.title: Microsoft Assets and Foundry Local Architecture
sections.summary: Describes Microsoft's existing assets (Azure AI Foundry, ONNX Runtime, Windows scale) combined into Foundry Local. Architecture includes ONNX Runtime at base, management service for model hosting, Azure AI Foundry connectivity, CLI, and SDKs. Available on Windows and macOS with hardware vendor partnerships. Over 100 private preview customers.

sections.title: Customer Testimonials
sections.summary: Two customer testimonials: Pieces CEO Savo describes migrating from Llama.cpp/Ollama to Foundry Local with improvements in memory management, time to first token, and tokens per second. Another customer demonstrates hybrid solutions combining Foundry Local with local speech-to-text for sensitive data scenarios.

sections.title: CLI Demo and Model Running
sections.summary: Live demo of Foundry Local CLI: model list showing hardware-specific variants, cache list of pre-downloaded models, running Phi-3.5 1.5B (~90 tokens/sec) and Phi-4 mini (better quality, slightly slower). Demonstrates model selection tradeoffs between performance and quality.

sections.title: Cross-Platform App Demo
sections.summary: Demonstrates a cross-platform document summarization app using JavaScript SDK with Foundry Local manager and endpoint. Same code runs on Windows and macOS with different model choices. Brief mention of local agent capability using local models and MCP servers.

sections.title: Local Agent Demo and Conclusion
sections.summary: Detailed demo of local agent capability using foundry agent commands. An OCR agent consisting of Phi-3.5 mini model and two MCP servers (file system and OCR mini) autonomously finds a receipt, extracts text via OCR, and computes the total amount. Ning concludes by noting local models are generally less capable than cloud models but unlock significant potential, and shares links for more information and private preview sign-up.
